name: markdown-sections-as-symbols
body: Markdown headings must map to graph symbols: each heading becomes a Struct section symbol, nested by heading level — a heading is contained by the file when it is the document's top level, or by the nearest lower-level heading otherwise (the schema nests symbols only through Struct, so a section is a Struct). The FQN scheme must be injective by construction, because the ingestor panics on any residual FQN collision rather than overwriting (SPEC §4). The scheme is anchored on the file's absolute path, never on a dot-joined directory/file-stem prefix: a markdown Module's FQN is the directory's absolute path; a markdown File's FQN is the file's absolute path, so the extension is retained and `docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` are distinct; a top-level section's FQN is `<file-fqn>.<section>`; a nested section extends its parent section's FQN as `<parent-section-fqn>.<section>`. Absolute paths are unique per file, so this keeps module and file prefixes disjoint and never renders two same-stem files (or two directories) to the same section FQN. Dot-joining a directory path is explicitly rejected as the lossy alternative that aliases `docs/guide` and `docs.guide` to the same `docs.guide` prefix. The exact slug rule that turns heading text into a name segment is an open design point (see the open-points note); it must be delimiter-safe — a slug maps heading text to one segment and never embeds the `.` separator ambiguously — and must map duplicate headings in one file to distinct segments. AC: a document with nested headings yields one Struct per heading, each contained by the correct parent; the same-stem fixture (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown`, each with a `## Overview`) and the path-alias fixture (`docs/guide/x.md` and `docs.guide/x.md`) yield distinct section FQNs and no ingestor FQN-collision panic.
